state:
**Goal `ext-intl`, Stage 4: one check is left. The plural agreement test with `Core\Cldr` still fails, now only because ICU4X has no data for some languages.** `format-numbers` (`extensions/intl/src/numbers.rs`) and `plural-categories` (`extensions/intl/src/plurals.rs`) are implemented, and both Stage 4 cases pass. `Core\Cldr` now follows CLDR 46 for `ro` cardinal, `is` cardinal, `scn` cardinal and ordinal (new `OrdinalSet::Ligurian`), the `gd` ordinal (new `OrdinalSet::ScottishGaelic`), the `lij` ordinal and the `az` ordinal on fractions (it reads `i`). `tests/conformance/core/cldr-plural-and-ordinal-rules-follow-current-cldr.nvst` pins one row for each.

`plural_rules_agree_with_core_cldr_on_its_whole_roster` (`crates/nvs-ext/tests/intl.rs`) is still `#[ignore]`d. Run it with `cargo test --test intl -- --ignored plural_rules_agree`. Every line it prints now has the same cause: ICU4X's baked plural data (`icu_plurals_data` 2.3) has no rules for about 70 languages on `Core\Cldr`'s roster, so it returns `Other`. These include `asa`, `bem`, `gv`, `kw` (cardinal *and* ordinal, so `kw` was never a stale `Core\Cldr` row), `prg`, `shi`, `tl`, `tzm` and `yi`. `mo` and `sh` are deprecated aliases that ICU4X does not canonicalize. ADR 0277 § 5 assumed ICU4X carries every language on the roster, and that is not true.

next.title: numbers and plural rules, the agreement

items.text: **Give the guest plural rules for every language on the roster.** Owned by ADR 0277 § 5. The recommended path is baking `PluralsCardinalV1` and `PluralsOrdinalV1` for the missing locales with full CLDR coverage (icu4x-datagen at the pinned version), in `extensions/intl/Cargo.toml:19` and at the constructor in `extensions/intl/src/plurals.rs:32`. Map `mo` to `ro` and `sh` to `sr-Latn` before the lookup. Record the size it adds.
**Remove the `#[ignore]`** at `crates/nvs-ext/tests/intl.rs:465` once the test passes. That closes the Stage 4 check.
